_comment: CB-8: health potions dropped by enemies. Every number here is tuning; code keeps only the rarity taxonomy. `rarities` is the canonical order (weakest first) and every table below must cover exactly those keys.

drop_chance._comment: chance = floor + (cap - floor) * t^exponent, where t is the enemy's BASE hp (data, never the run-time hp_mult) log-normalised between hp_min and hp_max and clamped to 0..1. hp_min/hp_max are the weakest and strongest non-boss enemies. The exponent keeps fodder low so the cap stays meaningful -- without it Husk-class trash sits near 10% and, being most of the kills, would be the whole potion economy.

enemy_rarity_hp._comment: Lower bound of each band on the enemy's BASE hp; anything under the `uncommon` bound is common. Potion rarity is decided by HP and by nothing else (owner, 2026-09-17: "potions can keep the same check by hp"). It used to be tied to `is_elite` as well -- the rule was "the rare band is exactly the elite enemies" -- and that rule is RETIRED as of G1, because elite became a tag five enemies carry rather than a description of the two toughest: Hexcaller (64) and Gorehorn (55) are elites that sit in the uncommon band, and that is intended, not a bug to bound around. `test_the_rare_band_is_exactly_the_elite_enemies` was deleted rather than re-pinned. Each bound sits near the MIDDLE of the hp gap it divides rather than on an enemy: uncommon splits teleporter 36 from charger 55, rare splits summoner 87 from Ravager 125. Was 40 / 125, where 125 was elite's exact hp -- a trap, because shaving a point off elite in a rebalance would silently drop it to the uncommon band and let it roll common potions, breaking a hard rule with no obvious cause. `test_no_enemy_sits_exactly_on_a_band_edge` now guards that.

rarity_weights._comment: enemy rarity -> relative weights over potion rarity, rolled only once a drop has been won. The two zeroes are the user's hard rules: a common enemy never drops a rare potion, a rare enemy never drops a common one.
